newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits steady to higher before GDP.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits steady to higher before GDP.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were steady to higher in the morning, dealers said on Friday.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of today's issue of the U.S. first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP), April new home sales, May Chicago purchasing managers index (PMI) and the May University of Michigan consumer sentiment index.
U.S. first-quarter gross domestic product is forecast to show an increase of 6.0 percent compared with a 5.6 percent gain reported in the previous quarter.
New homes sales for April are expected to be around 800,000 units, lower than 813,000 units in March.
The May Chicago PMI is expected to be around 56.8 percent against April's 57.2 percent.
The May University of Michigan index is expected to be around 104.0 from its previous month's 101.4.
"The market was dead. However settlement was higher with terms high. The dealers are waiting for next week's unemployment numbers. Weekly terms are quiet," a local dealer said.
"The market was very quiet in the morning," another dealer said.
In short dates, weekend rose 1/8 percentage point to 5-3/4 5-1/8 percent and Monday/Tuesday rose 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
Week-fixed were unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.

Among term rates, one month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent, nine months unchanged at 6-1/8 6 percent and twelve months percent unchanged at 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent.
